source_call_review.bootstrap_closures: Extracted from tests/test_filters.py lines 59-73 / experiments/lgssm/*.py lines 63-80. Generalisations checked: (a) transition noise rnds @ chol(Q).T: equals the test's elementwise (trans_cov ** 0.5).T for diagonal Q (asserted bitwise for a 2-D diagonal Q; PF results bitwise equal to the elementwise-root closure), Cholesky as in diffres.tools.simulate_lgssm; for non-diagonal Q the elementwise root would not be a covariance factor, so Cholesky is the correct generalisation. (b) observation density: diagonal R keeps the upstream sum of univariate norm.logpdf (bitwise vs upstream form on a 2-D diagonal-R model); non-diagonal R uses vmap(diffres.tools.logpdf_mvn_chol) (bitwise vs a direct closure using logpdf_mvn_chol and vs an independent jax.scipy.stats.multivariate_normal oracle on a dx=2, dy=3 full-R/full-Q/full-P0 model). (c) Branch switch: on the same diagonal-R model, wrapper diagonal branch vs wrapper full branch (R with 1e-300 off-diagonal) differ by 7.1e-15 in nll, 1.4e-14 in log-weights, 0 in particles; upstream-sum vs logpdf_mvn_chol closures differ identically. Both reduce exactly to the upstream code on all upstream models (all saved upstream nll values reproduced bitwise).
source_call_review.nll_offset: Confirmed from feynman_kac.py lines 81-85: nll0 = -logsumexp(log g0) without +log N, later increments use normalised weights, so raw nll = -log p_hat - log N exactly. Tested: H = 0 model (all potentials equal, PF likelihood exact): nll_plus_log_n equals the closed-form/KF nll to 1e-12 and nll = KF nll - log N for N = 16 and 100. Raw nll is returned as 'nll' (upstream value); nll_plus_log_n is a correctly labelled convenience.
source_call_review.kl_bures: Confirmed against diffres/tools.py lines 41-63: kl() = tr(S1^-1 S0) - d + quad + logdet S1 - logdet S0 = 2 KL(N0||N1) (tested vs numpy closed form, rel 1e-10); bures() = |m0-m1|^2 + tr(S0+S1-2(S0^1/2 S1 S0^1/2)^1/2) = squared W2 (tested vs commuting closed form). Wrapper calls kl(m_KF, P_KF, m_PF, P_PF) as experiments/lgssm/diffusion.py line 121, so the stated '2 * KL(N_KF || N_PF)' is correct.
